questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Corona did definitely affect my choice of destination. Norway is a country similar to Denmark and it has a good health care system. I love hiking and the wild nature in Norway. 
From an academic perspective, I chose UiO because they offer research projects for exchange students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Is was ill and used most of the time in my flat room. This affected the stay strongly.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find everything and the student organization at UiO helped with info for a student card, housing etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got emails with info and an account at SiO, the student organization at UiO, that has info about everything relating to living in Oslo as a student.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: SiO has different campuses not paced at the university but in small student cities. There were a shopping option, a large laundry room, and a student cafe/bar driven by volunteers. The city was really nice with a lot of different events but the flat I lived in did not have good facilities. I lived with 6 other exchange students charing a small kitchen and one bathroom.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In my flat, there was a shared, very small, kitchen with no limited supply and no dishwasher. But you could cook if wanted to.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The campuses "studentbyer" are very different some of them have nice facilities in the flat kitchen and you can get your own bathroom others were like my flat. But you get to know many other exchange students and they make many social events for the exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: UiO has a website, "studentweb", where you register courses you want to take. you also find grades and transcripts there.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have an email service I could contact.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want to do a research project, you need to make an agreement with a research group prior to registration. I made an agreement three months before I arrived.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I did one course; industrial pharmacy. It was project orientated which was really nice and challenging to do an academic project with people that have another knowledge base than myself. The academic level was not the highest. The course was not designed to give new academic knowledge but to gain skills in working in collaboration across different knowledge fields within the pharmaceutical industry.
The research project I did was definitely challenging and with a high academic level. It was about specialized pro-resolving lipid mediators that are discussed in the literature because the direct effect is still not completely elucidated.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was really nice that they are more project orientated than at UCPH. They used the same platform for information (canvas) which made it easy to understand and find information.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
FARM5110- Industrial pharmacy (10 ECTS)
FRM5020- Pharmaceutical research project (20 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
FRM5020- Pharmaceutical research project (20 ECTS)
It was really nice to see how they work in research groups in other countries.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I used money on traveling in Norway.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport is expensive and food as well. I did not use any money on books because they were provided by the professors online for free.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a student cafe/bar in the student village and they hosted different events like 17. may, BBQs, winter Olympics, etc. The student organization did also have fitness centers around the city and at the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The fitness is really cheap (200 DKK) and they have nice classes and water activities as well. You can also rent cross-country skis for free.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: To go for a hike. It is really easy to get out of the city by public transport and go for hikes in the mountains. Also to go by public boats to the islands in the fjord surrounding Oslo.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy, their culture is very close to the danish. However, everything is closed on Sundays and no one does any kind of work or readings on Sundays.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I was mostly interacting with master students in the research group I did my project.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everything is closed on Sundays and no one does any kind of work or readings on Sundays.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are better at doing breaks on the weekends and going on trips to nature. They are not as stressed as we are in Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy your time! Make sure to see some of the country! The nature is amazing. Make sure to socialize with you flatmates and with other students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The weather is cold for a long time and the days are short in the winter. In the summer period, the dark hours are short.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: When I had the time to go for trips, like skiing or hiking

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I was ill for a long time (two months). It was really difficult to catch up with the courses and be social. However, the university and research group was really nice to help me!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
